name: Keyframed Saturation Shift
use_when: A clip needs a visible mood shift from color to desaturated or black-and-white.
A memory, flashback, failure, reveal, emotional drop, or before/after beat benefits from a gradual color change.
The editor wants a simple mobile-friendly color transition without a full grade pass.
avoid_when: The color shift has no story, mood, or information job.
Skin, product colors, brand colors, captions, or evidence become harder to read.
A hard cut to a graded shot would communicate the change more clearly.

timeline_pattern.motivation_rule: Name the emotional or informational reason for the shift before applying it.
timeline_pattern.spacing_rule: Farther keyframes create a gradual mood shift; closer keyframes create a sudden impact.
timeline_pattern.property_rule: Only saturation should move when the beat is a black-and-white shift; do not keyframe hue, brightness, exposure, or filter values unless they also serve the beat.
timeline_pattern.restore_rule: If the story returns to normal, keyframe saturation back deliberately instead of leaving a hidden drift.

motion.rule: No direct motion rule; avoid pairing the color shift with extra motion unless both support the same beat.

sound.rule: A music dip, hit, or ambience change can support the shift only when it does not bury speech.

captions.rule: Caption contrast must be checked during both the color and desaturated states.

color.rule: Preserve readable faces, proof, captions, and product/brand information through the entire transition.

keyframe_values.capcut_example: A strong black-and-white shift can keyframe saturation down to about -50 in CapCut, then adjust by eye for skin/proof readability.
keyframe_values.fast_bw_hit: A fast CapCut black-and-white hit can happen over roughly 6-10 frames, including a 9-frame style spacing, when the shift is meant to feel sudden.
keyframe_values.subtle_shift: Use a smaller saturation reduction when the scene needs mood change without looking like a filter gag.

implementation.ffmpeg: Animate saturation with eq=saturation expressions or split sections with xfade/curves; render before/after stills for readability.
implementation.remotion: Interpolate filter saturation or CSS/filter values across frame ranges and store restore frames explicitly.
implementation.blender: Keyframe saturation or color-management values in the compositor when a rendered scene needs the effect.
implementation.capcut_equivalent: Add a starting keyframe with current adjustment values, move ahead, lower saturation, preview speed, and adjust spacing or restore keyframes.
implementation.premiere_equivalent: Keyframe Lumetri saturation or use an adjustment layer with opacity/keyframed effect strength; check scopes and captions.

common_mistakes: Using desaturation as a random style change without story motivation.
Changing saturation so quickly that the viewer reads it as a glitch.
Accidentally changing hue, brightness, or exposure when the intended move is only a saturation drop.
Leaving skin, products, maps, or evidence muddy after the shift.
Forgetting to restore color when the story returns to normal.
Letting captions lose contrast in the desaturated state.
qc: Can the editor name why the color shift happens at this beat?
Does the transition speed match the intended mood or impact?
Do faces, products, proof, and captions remain readable during the whole shift?
Is the saturation restored or held intentionally?
Does the effect avoid banding, flicker, or compression ugliness?
